question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what phase of the scan is being performed, and what is the immediate objective?
A. Switching to color Doppler to confirm vascularity and differentiate vessels from adjacent ducts or cystic structures
B. Rotating the probe into an orthogonal transverse plane to confirm the finding and assess cross-sectional anatomy
C. Probe alignment and initial view acquisition so the organ’s long axis is properly captured
D. End-to-end caliper placement along the visualized structure to obtain a maximum length measurement for documentation
groundtruth: The operator obliques the transducer to match the kidney’s natural oblique lie, then proceeds to obtain the standard long-axis kidney view for orientation.

question:

A. Fine-tune depth, gain, and focal zone to optimize a single-organ view for parenchymal detail without prioritizing adjacent landmarks.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what major probe reorientation is performed, and why?
A. Tilt (heel-toe) the probe to correct anisotropy and optimize echogenicity without changing imaging plane.
B. Rotate the probe to switch from a long-axis view to a perpendicular (short-axis) view
C. Rotate the probe 90° to convert a short-axis view into a long-axis (in-plane) view for continuous visualization along the structure.
D. Rock the probe to center the target and bring adjacent anatomy into view while maintaining the same axis.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what is the primary purpose of the continuous end-to-end sweep in the new plane?
A. Estimate organ volume by sweeping through the organ to allow off-line volumetric reconstruction
B. Ensure the entire organ is captured from its superior extent to its inferior extent
C. Confirm a suspected focal lesion by imaging it dynamically through the organ in a single plane
D. Obtain a cine loop to assess respiratory motion and reduce motion artifact with breath-hold coaching
groundtruth: In the transverse window, the operator sweeps all the way from the superior portion down to the inferior portion of the left kidney to visualize its full transverse extent.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what strategy is used to restore a clear view when image quality is limited?
A. Switch to a lower-frequency curvilinear probe to improve penetration when the target is poorly visualized
B. Apply firm graded compression and use small probe tilts to displace overlying soft tissue and reduce artifact
C. Reposition into a window between bony structures and sweep through that gap
D. Increase overall gain and adjust depth/focus to optimize near-field resolution before reacquiring the view
groundtruth: When the transverse picture is obscured, the operator scans through an intercostal space to avoid rib shadows and improve visualization of the upper or lower pole.

inference_metadata.raw_response: B. Apply firm graded compression and use small probe tilts to displace overlying soft tissue and reduce artifact
